tagline: Thirty-six miles across a county that kept supplying governors.
intro: The trail starts at the crossroads in Clio, where Highways 10 and 51 meet, and runs northeast through Louisville to the courthouse town of Clayton, then out Highway 30 to Eufaula on the Chattahoochee. It ends on US 431 at the Shorter Mansion, about 36 miles on.

Barbour County gave Alabama six governors and two acting ones, from John Gill Shorter, who helped write the Confederate constitution, to George Wallace, born in Clio, whose stand at the entrance of the University of Alabama to uphold segregation is still remembered, and Lurleen Wallace after him.

moments.title: Louisville
moments.text: Spelled Louisville and still pronounced Lewisville, a small town that has served as county seat for two different counties.

moments.title: Clayton
moments.text: County seat since the 1830s, laid out around a courthouse square, and known for a tombstone in the shape of a whiskey bottle that made Ripley's Believe It or Not.

moments.title: Shorter Mansion
moments.text: A Classical Revival house rebuilt after an 1895 fire, it went at auction in 1965 to a heritage association formed to buy and restore it, which held the town's first pilgrimage the next year.
